technique: Deconversion fee schedule disclosed in contract
description: Core processor contracts carry a separate deconversion fee schedule; regulators expect contracts to assign all costs and obligations of transition and termination, with reasonable time frames and data return.
measured_outcome: Jack Henry FY2025 deconversion revenue $33.905m (FY2024 $16.554m), deconversion costs $6.242m; most of it arises when a client agrees to be acquired. Interagency TPRM guidance (2023) asks banks to weigh termination costs and fees. Consultant ranges of $150k-$500k per bank and default terms of 100% of remaining-term fees are single-source claims.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH (inverse use): Unbound can publish its own exit and deconversion price schedule plus an export format as a sales asset. Incumbent DAF platform terms are already documented as opaque in the 10/13 series.

technique: Exit-fee litigation as a switching barrier signal
description: Credit unions are suing Fiserv to void early-termination and deconversion fees, generally pleading breach as the ground for exit.
measured_outcome: Polam FCU v. Fiserv: motion to dismiss denied 2026-06-18. Four other credit unions have similar suits pending; Fiserv has settled three. FiCare alleges seven-figure termination and deconversion fees. No fee figure has been adjudicated.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: shows that exit friction becomes a reputational and legal liability for an incumbent, which supports Unbound's symmetric-exit position. It is not evidence that buyers switch because of it.
evidence_class: VERIFIED-FACT (trade press reporting of court rulings)

technique: Multiple mock conversions before go-live with readiness criteria
description: The vendor runs full data conversions into a test environment one or more times, with predefined go-live readiness criteria and contingency plans if go-live slips.
measured_outcome: Practitioner guidance says 'at least two' mocks. Case examples: Vibrant CU ran 2 mocks (Dec 2015, Jan 2016); a reconversion ran mocks in Sep and Nov ahead of a Dec 12 live date. Georgia DBF guidance requires go-live readiness criteria to be predefined. No industry-wide statistic exists.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: matches the rehearsal discipline already in 11/17. Adds two mocks as the practitioner floor for DAF.
evidence_class: VERIFIED-FACT (regulator guidance text); VENDOR-CLAIM/case anecdotes (mock counts)

technique: Long-lead contract-expiry planning
description: Institutions start re-evaluating their core 18-24 months before the contract expires. Synergent advises starting the search 2 years before expiry. Conversion projects run about a year.
measured_outcome: SafeAmerica: a 'near yearlong' conversion. ICBA: 36% of banks were on their current core for 5 years or less in 2020, versus 13% in 2016; 34% had been on it 20+ years.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: the DAF sales trigger is the incumbent contract end date. The T0 assessment should capture that date and offer a back-scheduled plan.

technique: Reusable conversion program per source system ('off the shelf' vs written)
description: Core vendors reuse a conversion program when they have already converted from the same source core. A first conversion from a new source needs the program to be written.
measured_outcome: Qualitative only. Trade press says SafeAmerica was the first credit union to move from its legacy core to Corelation, so the program had to be written rather than 'pulled off a shelf' (search snippet). Same-vendor (Symitar to Symitar) conversions still needed product surveys for mapping. Data conversion cost is quoted at '$20,000 to $250,000' (single snippet).
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: direct support for a per-source-platform adapter (reusable) plus a per-sponsor mapping (product and fund-type survey) split.

technique: Year-to-date balance import plus prior-quarter tax verification
description: On a mid-year switch the new provider imports YTD payroll by employee and by quarter, plus current-year 941s. It checks the previous quarter's tax history for errors before the first live payroll.
measured_outcome: No measured outcome. ADP's guide lists the required artefacts and steps. A January 1 switch avoids the YTD import entirely.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: equivalent to the DAF cutover-year contribution and grant YTD needed for donor statements and 1099/acknowledgement continuity (complements IRS Rev. Proc. 2004-53 in 11). Also suggests a 'verify prior period' step at intake.

technique: Parallel payroll before first live run
description: After import, the new provider runs a parallel payroll beside the old one, and the first live payroll must match it. The old contract is closed only after the first successful live run.
measured_outcome: No published match-rate statistic. Paycor's countdown places parallel tests at about 30 days before go-live. Typical implementations are 8-16 weeks; 4-8 weeks is claimed for a 500-employee firm coming from ADP or Paylocity.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: DAF analogue is a shadow grant-cycle run comparing grant batches and fund balances. It is affordable because DAF volumes are small (11 already proposes a parallel run; this adds the 'keep the old contract until the first live cycle' rule).

technique: Competitor-report import adapters (named source + named report)
description: The new provider accepts specific standard reports from named competitors (ADP Run Employee Summary PDF and Payroll Details PDF; QuickBooks Online/Desktop; Paychex in beta) and parses them automatically. Pay items and deductions are configured separately.
measured_outcome: No accuracy figure. The upload is available only during onboarding. Masked fields in competitor exports do not import. Marketing shows a sample timeline with data import on days 3-5.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: strongest analogue for a DAF 'adapter per incumbent standard report' catalogue (NPact/FIMS, Ren DFX, Foundant reports). It works without incumbent cooperation because it consumes reports the customer can already download. That matches 13 §2a (Extraction Plan).

technique: Explicit cutover-period ownership of filings
description: The parties agree in writing who files the final quarter's 941 and state returns and who issues W-2s/1099s, to avoid duplicates.
measured_outcome: No measured outcome. Duplicate W-2s are cited as the failure mode.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: maps to the single issuer of cutover-year donor acknowledgements and 1099s for grants (already in 11 §5.4). Confirms that a RACI per regulatory artefact is standard practice.

technique: Negative-consent bulk transfer with 30-day notice
description: Accounts move in bulk without each customer re-papering. Customers get at least 30 days' notice with an opt-out and any cost disclosed. FINRA stopped pre-reviewing letters from 2026-04-01.
measured_outcome: Schwab-TDA Labor Day 2023 wave: more than 7,000 RIA firms, 3.6m accounts, $1.3T. Negative-consent notice sent end of June. Advisors could set up access from June 21. 4-5% of former TDA RIAs left (Schwab: roughly as projected). Reported issues: logons, account titles in third-party tools, '2 1099s'. DocuSign client process went from about 2 hours to about 30 seconds (Schwab claim).
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM-LOW: there is no DAF statutory basis for negative consent. The sponsor owns the funds, so donor consent is not needed for a platform change (same sponsor). Useful pattern: advance notice plus pre-cutover credential setup window plus opt-out only for ProgramTransfer cases. Needs counsel review.
evidence_class: VERIFIED-FACT (FINRA notice summary; trade press figures); VENDOR-CLAIM (Schwab metrics)

technique: Pre-cutover access provisioning window
description: Users of the receiving platform get credentials and training about 10 weeks before the conversion weekend, so day-one login issues are limited to the residual.
measured_outcome: Schwab: access from 2023-06-21 for a 2023-09-02..05 conversion. Residual logon problems were still reported at one firm.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: provision sponsor staff and advisor identities (SCIM, as in 11) and run a training tenant before cutover. Measure the percentage of users activated before cutover as a readiness gate.

technique: Old-to-new ID mapping file plus 10-business-day import SLA once valid data is received
description: The receiving processor publishes an SLA that starts when valid data arrives. The data is PGP-encrypted over SFTP, then validated. The customer approves a validation summary, which includes confirming last-4 digits for 2 customers. A mapping file is returned. Volume is ramped after the merchant ID changes.
measured_outcome: SLA: 10 business days after valid data; more than 1M records may take longer; Bacs 4-6 weeks. The previous processor's export takes 'days to months', which is the dominant variable. Data Transfer Agreements 'significantly lengthen' timelines. Card verification codes, subscriptions and invoices are excluded.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: copy the clock-starts-on-valid-data SLA, the customer-approved validation summary with spot checks, and the explicit exclusions list. Mapping file and ramping are already covered in 11; the new items here are the validation-summary approval and published exclusions.

technique: Statistical-sampling validation of migrated data
description: Validate migrated records with per-data-type statistical samples at 98% confidence and 0.2-1% error limits, instead of fixed 10-20% manual review.
measured_outcome: No errors found in migrated data over 12 months after go-live (clinician-reported). A 15% echo check (4,932 reports) found 1 error, within limits. Estimated saving of 56k-115k person-hours versus 10-20% samples; provider notes needed 1,695 samples instead of 316,845 (about $3.68m at $70/h). The only gap was about 6,000 notes out of scope.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH for non-financial fields (donor names, addresses, advisor links, grant memo text). NOT for balances: financial fields need 100% control totals (16). Use sampling for attribute-level validation and full reconciliation for money.

technique: Selective conversion plus active archive of legacy data
description: Convert recent and key data (often 12-24 months of demographics and clinical elements) and keep the rest in a read-only, queryable archive. Leaving the legacy system running for lookup is ineffective.
measured_outcome: Thin literature (Schreiber & Garber 2020 review). One Swedish survey: 11% of users wanted everything converted; 30% wanted selected categories. The 12-24 month figure comes from an archive vendor.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: DAF donors expect full fund history (AEF/Ren 2-year visibility was criticised in 10/13). An archive tier with a donor-visible read-only history view is a fallback, not a default. Disclose as HistoryIncomplete.

technique: Performance measures for migrated-data quality before deployment
description: GAO recommended that VA set measures and goals for migrated data (accessibility, accuracy, appropriateness) before further deployments.
measured_outcome: Clinicians reported errors in allergy, medication and immunization data. A VA post-deployment report found patient-safety risk from incomplete migration. Recommendation still open; deployments paused until 2026.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: define sponsor-visible migrated-data quality metrics (per-fund balance tie-out, history completeness %, unmapped-field count) as acceptance gates, not post-hoc.

technique: Opening balances plus 2-3 years of summary trial balances; open items in detail
description: Migrate opening balances, per-period trial balances (often by journal per period), and open AR/AP/PO in detail. Older detail becomes balances. Cut over at year end or at least month end. Run at least two test migrations and tie out to the legacy trial balance.
measured_outcome: No measured outcome. History depth guidance varies: 6-12 months (Packt NetSuite book) to 2-3 years (partners); DataBlend includes 2 years by default and charges extra beyond that.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: DAF needs per-fund rather than GL-only continuity, so per-fund opening balance plus history (14 Option C) is stronger than ERP practice. Adopt: cut over at period end, at least 2 test migrations, tie-out to the legacy fund trial balance.

technique: Predefined migration objects/templates with auto-mapping
description: The vendor ships a library of target-side migration objects, each with a template. Source data is filled into the template and mapped automatically to target structures.
measured_outcome: SAP slide claims a 70% overall effort reduction versus LSMW (vendor claim, third-party copy, 2022). No independent measurement.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: this is the 'target-side canonical package' half of the split (Unbound Migration Package / CMM in 14). The figure is VENDOR-CLAIM and must not be used as a forecast.

technique: Closed-block conversion to specialist administrator
description: A carrier whose administrator was exiting moved a UL/VUL block to a specialist policy administration system and TPA, with a pre-conversion data archive that remains reportable.
measured_outcome: About 40,000 active plus 80,000 inactive policies; ready for conversion in under 12 months (project began May 2012). No mock or reconciliation details published.
transfer_to_daf: LOW-MEDIUM: analogous to a sponsor outsourcing a run-off DAF program. The 'inactive records kept in reportable archive' element supports a tiered history approach.

technique: LLM/ML schema-mapping suggestions with deterministic constraint gate and human verification
description: Rank candidate source-to-target field matches, then filter them with constraints and human review.
measured_outcome: Valentine (ICDE 2021): schema-only matchers have low effectiveness and are sensitive to noisy names. BDIViz: 93% of true matches appear in the top-10 candidates, but the LLM validator misclassifies up to 38%. Monka et al. 2026: F1 rises from 0.08 to 0.66 with a constraint gate; macro-F1 0.70 on 7 enterprise datasets; about 7x lower expert effort than spreadsheets. Parciak et al. 2024: the healthcare benchmark has 49 true matches among 1,839 pairs; both too little and too much context hurt.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH as an assistant only. Evidence supports 'AI proposes, deterministic gates and human dispose' (Transitus DF-TRN-0012; 13). Expect about 0.7 F1, not autonomy. Recall@10 is high, so present ranked suggestions.

technique: Free or guaranteed migration as acquisition offer
description: Vendors bundle free data transfer with a new contract: DonorPerfect (switch before 2026-06-30 with a 2-year plan); DataBank (free migration up to 20,000 contacts); Keela (free guided onboarding); Givebutter 'Magic Migration'; Gusto free migration support.
measured_outcome: No vendor publishes the conversion lift. The offers are time-limited and tied to a minimum term, which suggests they are used as a closing incentive.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: common in adjacent nonprofit software, so a free migration alone is not a differentiator. The differentiator would be a published, verifiable outcome (see 11 ADVB-12).

technique: Pre-sale proof of concept / technical win
description: Run a scoped proof of concept or data assessment before the contract.
measured_outcome: Vivun benchmark: POCs average 33 days. PreSales Pulse 2026 (38 companies, 412 SE responses, unverified method): median POC win rate 62% for horizontal SaaS, 44% fintech, 38% healthcare. Overall B2B win rates are 20-47% depending on source. No migration-assessment-specific study found. Foundant's pre-contract POC is not confirmed: its support page was 403 to this agent and search found only an 'outset migration' after contract.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: directional evidence that a POC correlates with higher win rates, but selection bias applies (POCs are offered to qualified deals). The causal effect for DAF is UNKNOWN; Unbound should instrument it.

technique: Paid assessment credited against implementation
description: Charge for an assessment and credit part of the fee to the first invoice if the buyer proceeds. The example credits 60%.
measured_outcome: No outcome data.
transfer_to_daf: MEDIUM: an option for T2-T3 assessments (13) to filter out tyre-kickers while removing the cost for buyers who sign.

technique: Buyer lock-in concern as purchase barrier
industry: Enterprise platforms (BCG 2025 survey via Univ. of Auckland)
description: Survey of client firms on platform switching concerns.
measured_outcome: Technical migration cost worried 75% of respondents, productivity loss 64%, transition downtime 63%. 77% keep their own data model rather than the platform's, to preserve switching options.
transfer_to_daf: HIGH: supports leading with exit symmetry (sponsor-owned data model and export) alongside onboarding, because buyers anticipate the next switch.
